influences.name: The Band
influences.context: Originally from Minneapolis, lead singer Craig Finn and lead guitarist Tad Kubler formed The Hold Steady In 2003 when watching The Band concert film The Last Waltz. Finn asked Kubler, "Dude, why aren't there any bands like this anymore?" and they realised something had to be done.

influences.name: Bruce Springsteen
influences.context: Picture Finn as a non-creepy Woody Allen figure singing Springsteen songs, and you have the right idea.

influences.name: Thin Lizzy
influences.context: There's power, the crunch and the sheer volume of twin guitars – for example in the Thin Lizzy style guitars of Southtown Girls.

influences.name: Iggy Pop
influences.context: Did you see that Stooges documentary? When Iggy's talking about the difference between Ron [Asheton] and James Williamson, he's like 'James is like a rabid animal who gets into a room and gets into every little corner.' I play guitar like that.

influences.name: Steve Selvidge
influences.context: Steve is much more tasteful. I always call it 'the sprinkles'. He's definitely inspired me to try and play more like that, in a less-is-more kind of way.

influences.name: Chris Osgood
influences.context: I walked into my first day of lessons and my guitar teacher was Chris Osgood from The Suicide Commandos. So he taught me a lot about guitar and a lot about life.

influences.name: Wire
influences.context: I was certainly more into Wire and The Fall and things like that in my 20s. And that might reflect more on the Lifter Puller sound, and then there was this embrace of classic rock.

influences.name: The Fall
influences.context: I was certainly more into Wire and The Fall and things like that in my 20s. And that might reflect more on the Lifter Puller sound, and then there was this embrace of classic rock.

influences.name: Mark E. Smith
influences.context: And did listening to Mark E. Smith help you figure out, like, I could do it like this? Yeah, those kind of barking vocals made more sense in what I could do with my voice.

influences.name: The Rolling Stones
influences.context: Man, Let It Bleed is a way better record than all those other records that we were listening to!

influences.name: The Clash
influences.context: I think about The Clash: you'd always hear about these legendary shows, stories of Joe Strummer sneaking in their fans who couldn't afford it through the upstairs bathroom to get into the show.

influences.name: Tom Ruprecht
influences.context: A friend of mine, Tom Ruprecht, was a writer om Letterman. He told me how he hates movies that depict a writer with writer's block, just sitting there with a blank cursor or a blank page. He says, 'That would be nice, but my show is going on the air at 11:30, so I need to write a show, and then I need to make it good.' That really stuck with me

influences.name: Bob Dylan
influences.context: That's exactly what I do. I read. Read and pay attention to other artists, which might include listening to music. What does Bob Dylan do?

influences.name: Philip Roth
influences.context: That's exactly what I do. I read. Read and pay attention to other artists, which might include listening to music. What does Philip Roth say? Having another voice in my head gives me a spark.

influences.name: Jack Kerouac
influences.context: What literary figures inspire you as a songwriter? Kerouac, for one. I love reading him aloud; his words pop when you read them in the way a good set of lyrics should.

influences.name: Raymond Carver
influences.context: The other one is Raymond Carver, the way he can tell a story in such a minimalist style. For a songwriter, that's a huge thing.
